color.note: log10 of the showers per bin, empty bins transparent. A bin holding one shower is drawn at position 0.4 of Viridis, #29788e, 3.2:1 against the #1c2128 card: the ramp's own first colour, #440154, is 1.06:1 and would make a count of one disappear. Each offered palette has its own start in ramp.by_palette. Turbo darkens towards its end, so its peak is drawn at position 0.85, the last that clears 3:1.

axis.bin_rule: Freedman–Diaconis: bin width 2 · IQR · N^(−1/3), the widest among the drawn series so they share one binning, clamped to 8–120 bins over the axis. An exception to the Rice rule, for prediction residuals only: their tails are heavy, and a bin count set by the sample size alone spreads the core over a single bin of a range the tail sets, while the interquartile range follows the core

clipping.note: Display range covers the 1st to 99th percentile; 2 of 62 values (3.23%) lie outside it and are excluded from the view but not from the statistics.

axis.basis: pooled residuals of the showers with N ≥ 15

fit.estimator_note: Iterated ±2.5σ core refit over 47 of 62 events in 10 iterations; de-biased for truncation.
fit.note: Moment width 0.388 and robust width 0.0341 differ by 91%; this spectrum has a non-Gaussian tail and the fitted curve describes the core only.

interval.label: 95% Student-t interval of the mean, 61 dof

sigma.note: Non-Gaussian: robust (IQR) width 0.0341 against the moment width 0.388.

interval.label: 95% Student-t interval of the mean squared residual, 61 dof; square root of the MSE interval

notes.series: The shipped XGBoost regressor of this experiment's species and seed on the notebook's 20 % validation split (train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=42)), the rows it was not trained on; the selection applies to them, and the training rows it selects are counted in split.n_training_excluded, not drawn.
notes.pairs: Each count is an event. Below N = 15 pairs the individual (truth, prediction) pairs are drawn instead of a density, because a cell of one or two events would be set by the binning, not by the model.
notes.axes: Truth and prediction share one range taken from the whole event table, whatever the selection, so the identity line is the diagonal and the picture does not move when a filter changes. Events beyond it are counted in outside, never dropped silently.
notes.residual: The residual is the quantity of the model-performance card. Its range is the 1st to 99th percentile of the residuals when at least 20 are drawn (axis.clipping.applied); below that it is their full extent and axis.provisional is set. From N = 15 a series is a density histogram, which is its spread, with its fitted Gaussian; its mean is a long-dashed rule with the 95 % Student-t interval of the mean as two thin hairlines. Below N = 15 its events are drawn in a reserved band, with the mean's capped Student-t whisker and an uncapped ± 1 SD bar, the spread of the events: two marks, two quantities.
notes.calibration: The regressor predicts the momentum scale directly; no sampling-fraction calibration is applied.
notes.relative: A relative residual needs a positive truth; an event without one is left out and counted in residual.excluded.

split.rule: train_test_split(np.arange(n), test_size=0.2, random_state=42) over the event table in event_number order (the producer file's order)

validation / training MSE of the shipped model at random_state 42 must exceed 1.05 times the largest of the same ratio at 99 other random_state values (0 to 99 without 42): a model predicts the rows it was trained on better than the rest. The per-row errors come from one prediction of every row; each seed only re-indexes them.
